title: Premium Accounting Standard: Working Out the Return of Supplement Premium Charged Over Another Coverage
content:
This is the accounting basis on which a return of premium under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is worked out.

### 1. Where the figures come from

The return is worked out from the entries standing on the policy's premium account for the span in which the supplement took effect, never from the rate table, because what is given back is what was taken.

### 2. The months returned

The months returned are the months of that opening span on which the two coverages ran together. No month is counted as run together: premium is owed from the day the supplement took effect.

### 3. The value of a month

Each month counted is returned at the value of a month of the opening span. A month is valued at the amount posted for the opening span, taken in full.

### 4. What is returned with the premium

The premium alone is returned, and nothing is added for any other rate component.

### 5. What is deducted

Money the plan has already given back is never given back twice. Nothing is deducted from the return.

### 6. Putting the figures together

The months counted are multiplied by the value of a month together with the rate components returned with it, the deduction is taken from that product, the figure is rounded to the cent once at the end, and where the deduction exceeds the premium being returned nothing is returned and nothing further is owed.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a policy whose premium account carries one charge of 151.30 for the span in which the supplement took effect, paying for one month of cover. The months counted as run together are none, so 0 months are counted. A month of the opening span is valued at the amount posted for that span taken in full, being 151.30. Nothing is added for any other rate component, so the value returned for each month counted is 151.30. Nothing is deducted. The months counted, 0, multiplied by 151.30, give nothing, and the deduction of nothing leaves nothing. Rounded to the cent once at the end, the return is 0.00.
